findings.reason: the plan should name `runs.repair_manifest_status` as the owner to generalise (or say the generic `--set` replaces `repair-status`), otherwise §4 mints a second repair path that drifts from the first.
findings.text: §4's `crew repair-manifest --run R --set field=value` reimplements a mechanism that already exists: `repair_manifest_status()` retains `manifest.md.asdelivered`, rewrites the field and atomically replaces via `os.replace`, and it is already surfaced as `crew repair-status` (reckon/cli.py:6536). §4's declared write paths are `reckon/cli.py`, the sync implementation, the skills and tests — `runs.py` is not named, so the implementer must fork the mechanism or reach into an unlisted owner.

findings.reason: §3's rewiring is half-done; it retires the pointer-classification duplicate but leaves the resolver duplicate the immediately preceding section exists to eliminate, so the plan should name `crew path` as the resolver for the script too.
findings.text: §3 owns this script and its done-when requires it to call `crew list` and `crew claims` "with no local pointer-classification fallback", but it is silent on the file's own `config_home()` (lines 114–122), a byte-for-byte re-implementation of `reckon/_store.py::_config_home` (RECKON_HOME → `~/.config/reckon` → `~/docs-server`). §2 just landed `crew path --kind live|config-home` to remove exactly this coupling, and §1 calls config-home hardcoding the largest consumer coupling at 1,537 lines.

findings.reason: the section must either widen `crew claims` to carry worktree ownership or keep a facet of local derivation and say so, or the done-when cannot be met as written.
findings.text: §3's done-when has `worktree_fleet.py` call `crew claims` for its worktree claims, but `crew claims` (§3 text) "derives every claim from `node.write_paths`", whereas `live_worktree_claims()` keys the inventory on the pointer's `worktree` field (`pointer["worktree"]`). The verb named inventories write-paths; the script needs worktree→run ownership, so "no local pointer-classification fallback" is not reachable with the single verb the section names.

findings.reason: the section's own justification for the verb rests on a distinction the code contradicts, so the author must either correct the claim or state the real reason a CLI reader is needed (shell/batch consumers with no MCP).
findings.text: §3 states `crew lanes` "is expressly distinct from the endpoint/quota payload of MCP `view=\"lanes\"`", but that view already attaches the lane reading through `_attach_lane_document()` (called at mcp_views.py:1044 and 803/833), so headroom, running and the rest of the lane-document fields are already on the MCP surface. The plan adds a second reader of the same document without saying why the existing surface cannot serve consumers or be extended.

findings.reason: the section must state which existing command it replaces (`repair-status`) or why nothing can be retired, so the added CLI-option surface is accounted for in the section's own text.
findings.text: the section adds two CLI surfaces (`crew repair-manifest` with a free-form `--set field=value`, and `reckon sync --write`) and a near-duplicate of `crew repair-status`, yet names nothing it retires or merges among the `cli_options` family (317 this week). §4's "two coordinator recipes become verbs" retires prose, not CLI surface, and the recipes are outside all four counted families.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §4's repair verb hides the as-delivered copy, the canonical field shape, the `check-manifest` run and the atomic replace behind one command, and §2 delegates to the crew store's existing resolvers (`reports_dir`, `runs_dir`, `run_dir`, `live_dir`, `review_store_root`) rather than re-deriving the layout.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 adds a manifest-repair path parallel to `runs.repair_manifest_status`/`crew repair-status`, and §3 leaves `worktree_fleet.config_home()` — the exact config-home duplicate §2 built a verb to remove — in place.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §4 adds `crew repair-manifest` and `reckon sync --write` without naming what they retire or merge, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §1's census and §2–§3 cite the mechanisms they extend (`_config_home` in `reckon/_store.py`, `read_lane_document_file` in `reckon/crew/lane_document.py`, and `skills/reckon-build/scripts/worktree_fleet.py`), so the plan searched before proposing new surface.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3's `crew lanes` is a second reader of the lane document that MCP `view="lanes"` already attaches, and the plan's stated distinction from that view is not what the code does.
